clue.text: Work capacity that masses still have

definitions.text: Work capacity that masses still have

parts.words: Work capacity that masses still have
parts.note: surface reading: the output that crowds of people can still manage
setter's reading: physics, where bodies at rest still hold stored energy by their position

explanation.surface: A comment on how much labour the toiling crowds still have left in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Masses' suggests the working masses; read as physics, a still mass raised up carries stored energy, POTENTIAL ENERGY.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics, energy means the capacity to do work, and the stored kind belongs to objects by their position even while motionless.

clue.text: Sheet anchor?

parts.note: surface reading: a sheet anchor is a ship's large emergency anchor, or figuratively a mainstay
setter's reading: a small office item that anchors sheets of paper together

explanation.walkthrough: A sheet anchor is a nautical term for a spare heavy anchor; take 'sheet' as a page and the thing holding it is a PAPER CLIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent wire fastener holds loose pages together, literally keeping documents in place like a small mooring.

clue.text: Site of protest means quarantine is useless

indicators.note: something useless is broken and no good as it stands, so the letters must be rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written, all fifteen letters

explanation.surface: A protester argues that enforced isolation achieves nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The great Beijing plaza was where students demonstrated for reform in 1989 before the army crushed them.

clue.text: Require line to drop in bait

parts.note: to require something is to need it

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it fall away, so the word that follows is removed from the one before

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; these are the letters removed

explanation.surface: An angler needs fishing line to lower the bait into the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' and 'bait' pull towards fishing, but 'in' is the bit that drops out of LINE, leaving LE.
explanation.definitionFit: To bait someone is to taunt or provoke them, which is exactly what needling a person means.

clue.text: Bird is catching bird? No way!

indicators.note: catching means taking hold of, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: no here means without, so the following word's letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to believe a bird could catch another bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No way!' reads as disbelief, but it is an instruction: 'way' names a road to be taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a downcurved bill, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: New parts tangled in clumsy angler's gear

indicators.note: to part something is to split it open, so the first letter goes in between the others
a clumsy arrangement is awkward and jumbled, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A fumbling fisherman gets fresh pieces of kit snarled up in his tackle.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglers use a long-handled mesh bag to lift a hooked fish out of the water safely.

clue.text: Slowly eat beef, getting bill first

indicators.note: first places the word just before it at the front, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: a nib is a bird's beak, or bill
to beef is to complain, as is to bleat

explanation.surface: Someone working slowly through a plate of beef while the bill arrives early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' looks like the food being eaten, but here it is the verb meaning to grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking small bites over time is how one eats slowly and tentatively.

clue.text: Pelt of animals kept as pets

parts.words: Pelt of animals kept as pets
parts.note: surface reading: the fur or hide of a household pet

parts.words: Pelt of animals kept as pets
parts.note: setter's reading: pelt as heavy downpour, a shower made of the commonest pets

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pelt' looks like a skin, but it is the verb for falling hard; the idiom for a downpour names the two favourite pets.
explanation.definitionFit: To pelt down is to fall very heavily, and the idiom for a torrential downpour is exactly that.

clue.text: Peasant couple given pound

parts.note: to yoke is to couple or join together
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: A poor farm worker and his wife are handed a single pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustic country person of simple ways is a disparaging synonym for a farm labourer.

clue.text: It may look like 5, but it's a 2-digit figure

definitions.text: It may look like 5, but it's a 2-digit figure

parts.words: It may look like 5, but it's a 2-digit figure
parts.note: surface reading: a number puzzle, something resembling 5 that is really a two-digit number
setter's reading: a hand shape made with two fingers, which looks like the Roman numeral V

explanation.walkthrough: Digits are fingers as well as numerals; two fingers raised in a V look like the Roman five, giving PEACE SIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippie symbol of goodwill is two raised fingers spread apart, a gesture made with two digits.

clue.text: Open and close bass loop

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bass in music
a link is a loop in a chain

explanation.surface: Instructions for working a loop of bass guitar music on and off.
explanation.definitionFit: Shutting the eyes briefly and reopening them is what a quick flicker of the eyelids does.

clue.text: Join forces again, in fact

definitions.meaning: first meaning: RE- plus ALLY, to become allies once more

explanation.surface: Two sides decide to team up once more, and they actually do.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-ALLY, the word means to form an alliance anew.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb the word means actually or truly; split as a verb it means to form an alliance anew.

clue.text: Job description? Great!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Job is a book of the Old Testament, so describing it you would call it scriptural
second meaning: on a huge scale, as in floods of epic proportions

explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' at the start of the clue hides its capital: it is the Old Testament figure, not employment.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means drawn from scripture, and colloquially huge, as in disasters of enormous proportions.

clue.text: Run off opening businesses — very good area for wealth

indicators.note: opening means splitting apart, so the two firms part to take something between them

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, here two of them

indicators.note: off means wrong or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A businessman advises launching companies in a prosperous district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Businesses' supplies two companies, which open up to admit the jumbled run before the remaining pieces follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The horn of plenty symbolises abundance, so the word stands for a rich overflowing supply of riches.

clue.text: To hit — heavy or light

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang verb, to strike someone hard
second meaning: a device that gives illumination

explanation.surface: Someone choosing between a hard blow and a soft tap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy or light' looks like a choice of force, but 'light' is the second definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, to strike someone hard is to wallop them; separately, a bulb in a holder gives illumination.

clue.text: I'm not playing around with emotions

indicators.note: around here means messing about, so the letters are moved into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone insists they are not toying with anyone's feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing around' looks like one phrase, but 'playing' is fodder and 'around' alone signals the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in a deeply touching, moving way means doing so with strong feeling.

clue.text: Once you declare "I love you" by text, it's 11 12!

parts.note: ye is the old form of you
to aver is to declare or state firmly
ILY is the texting shorthand for these three words

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned lover texting an affectionate message is told it sounds very archaic.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 and 12 refer to the answers REALLY and BIBLICAL: a really biblical phrase is YEA VERILY. 'By text' tells you to use the texting abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the King James Bible's emphatic truly, so it is a really scriptural expression.

clue.text: In lodge, relaxing mostly, like to drink squash

indicators.note: drinking takes something inside, so one word swallows the other
mostly means not all of it, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: akin means like or similar
to squash is to press

explanation.surface: Skiers unwind in the chalet with a glass of fruit cordial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squash' is also a British fruit cordial, which suits the drinking surface; here it is the verb meaning to crush.
explanation.definitionFit: The French term covers the social unwinding at a ski resort after a day on the slopes.

clue.text: Was bouncer messaged about bad atmosphere?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes around the second

parts.note: to ping someone is to send them a quick message
a pong is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A nightclub doorman texts friends about the nasty mood inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncer' suggests a doorman, but here it is something that bounces back and forth like a table-tennis ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving rapidly back and forth like a table-tennis ball is behaving like something that bounces.

clue.text: Give a detailed account

parts.note: to give is to sag or yield under weight
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to report something thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as one instruction, but 'Give' is a verb meaning to droop.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, involved story recounting events at length is an epic narrative.

clue.text: Smashing up a Balkan's fencing

indicators.note: fencing encloses ground, so one word is put around the other

parts.note: a Serb is a native of Serbia in the Balkans; the 's is 'is'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man from the Balkans wrecks the fence around something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashing' looks like breaking things, but in British speech it means excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, smashing means excellent or wonderful, a near synonym.

clue.text: What Manuel said in scene about string

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second
about means turned round or in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
Manuel, the Spanish waiter in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers, constantly says 'Que?'

explanation.surface: A sitcom waiter comments on some string during a scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A series of things following one after another is a chain or run, which a string also means.

clue.text: As short girl gets up, dance

indicators.note: in a down entry, getting up means the letters read from bottom to top
short means cut off, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A petite young woman rises to her feet to join the dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a lively Latin American partner dance with Cuban roots.

clue.text: Master's membership reminder?

parts.note: a sub is a subscription, the fee for membership
a reminder says a payment is owing

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster receives a note that his club fees are owed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master's' looks possessive, but it is 'Master is', a verb defined by the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To master something is to overcome or conquer it, the same as bringing it under control.

clue.text: Echo around small part of church

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the first word wraps the following letter

parts.note: to ape is to copy or echo
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Voices reverberate through a little corner of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Echo' fits the church acoustics, but it is the verb meaning to mimic.
explanation.definitionFit: The semicircular vaulted recess at the east end of a church holds the altar.

clue.text: See commercials a lot

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
ads are commercials

explanation.surface: Someone who watches a great many television adverts.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial word for a great quantity or plenty of something.

clue.text: Before cooking one, go for a pizza topping

indicators.note: before here fixes order: the pieces named after it go at the front of the others

parts.note: go and pep both mean energy or vigour
per means for, as in so much per head
food that is cooking is on
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cook chooses a topping for one pizza before it goes in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' looks like time, but it means the pieces for 'go for' come before those for 'cooking one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spicy salami sliced and scattered over the cheese is one of the commonest toppings on pizzas.

clue.text: A mission for us, but only in capitals

definitions.text: A mission for us, but only in capitals

parts.note: surface reading: a task meant for ourselves
setter's reading: write us in capitals as US, the United States; such diplomatic missions sit in capital cities

explanation.walkthrough: 'In capitals' works twice: US in capital letters is the United States, and embassies are found in capital cities.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomatic mission is the official body representing a country abroad, here Washington's, housed in foreign capitals.
